entities.name: Maria
aliases: Lady Maria of the Astral Clocktower

facts.text: Maria came from the Cainhurst aristocratic bloodline, the tradition the church eventually sent Logarius to destroy.
Maria distanced herself from her Cainhurst heritage by choosing the path of a hunter instead of practicing vile blood arts.
Maria was taught by Gehrman and became skilled enough with the Rakuyo trick weapon to be considered the finest hunter he trained.
Maria shared use of the Rakuyo weapon with her companion Simon.
Maria was present at the fishing hamlet when scholars arrived and participated in or failed to prevent the killing of villagers and the desecration of Kos.
Before leaving the fishing hamlet, Maria threw her Rakuyo into the village well, symbolically rejecting the person she had been during the massacre.
After leaving the hamlet, Maria spent her remaining years at the Research Hall caring for patients, seeking some form of redemption.
Maria died at the Research Hall and was taken into the Hunter's Nightmare after death.
In the nightmare, Maria guards the Astral Clock Tower, which leads to the path to the fishing hamlet.
In the nightmare, Maria's Rakuyo is restored to her despite her having thrown it away in life.
In her nightmare boss fight, Maria bleeds from her own body into her attacks, using her Cainhurst blood in a way she would have found repellent in life.
When defeated, Maria whispers about failing and not being able to protect people, referring to children, villagers, and patients she could not save.
Kos's enormous body lies dead and preserved on the shore of the fishing hamlet nightmare, rendered into an object by the scholars who violated her.
The Orphan of Kos is born from inside the corpse of the great one Kos, emerging in front of the player trailing an umbilical cord.
The Orphan of Kos wields a weapon fashioned from its own placenta.
The sound the Orphan of Kos makes when it is born is the same audio file used for Gehrman crying in his sleep, which can be heard resting at the Hunter's Dream later in the story.
In its second phase, the Orphan of Kos abandons its placenta weapon and manifests ghostly wings, briefly showing the shape of the great one it might have grown into.
After the player kills the Orphan of Kos, the doll states that Gehrman is sleeping soundly for the first time in a long while.
Lawrence, the First Vicar, appears in the Hunter's Nightmare as a burning cleric beast in the Grand Cathedral, a nightmare duplicate of the cathedral he built.
Lawrence founded the Healing Church after leaving Byrgenwerth with the old blood, against Master Willem's warnings of overreach.
Unlike other clerics who gradually transform, Lawrence became the first cleric beast completely and absolutely.
The skull displayed on Vicar Amelia's altar in the waking world is not Lawrence's real skull, but a different creature's skull repurposed as a relic.
Lawrence's actual skull can be found inside the Grand Cathedral in the Hunter's Nightmare.
When the player brings Lawrence's real skull near his burning cleric beast form, the creature reaches toward it in recognition before the fight begins.
The scholars who violated the fishing hamlet are bound eternally in the Hunter's Nightmare as punishment.
Lawrence burns in the nightmare because he ordered the burning of Old Yharnam, incinerating a district and its inhabitants.
The item description of Lawrence's skull states it symbolizes his past and what he failed to protect, and that even if he found it, it could never restore his memories.
Gehrman waits in the Hunter's Dream, tending graves and greeting hunters, having done so through roughly 300 hunters according to in-game lore.
The Burial Blade was forged from caryll runes-adjacent ciderite (a metal that falls from the heavens) and was designed not for combat but for a funeral rite, a dirge of farewell.
Gehrman offers to use the Burial Blade to end the player's dream and grant them the same mercy he has given hundreds of hunters before.
Gehrman cannot use the Burial Blade's mercy on himself because the Moon Presence requires him to sustain the dream.
If the player refuses Gehrman's offer, he rises from his wheelchair and fights as the first hunter, using the art of quickening surrounded by blue luminescent fog.
When Gehrman is defeated in the boss fight, he reaches upward as if toward Maria, the woman whose loss is tied to his bargain with the dream.
The doll was made in the likeness of Maria, and Gehrman keeps her hair ornament by the workshop furnace.
If the player has consumed enough umbilical cord fragments to resist its call, the Moon Presence descends and a final battle begins against it directly.
Defeating the Moon Presence leads to the Childhood's Beginning ending, where the player becomes an infant great one held by the doll.
The Pthumerian civilization is depicted as having encountered the same cosmic truths explored by the Healing Church, with their answers buried in the chalice dungeons.
Byrgenwerth scholars uncovered the buried Pthumerian knowledge about the old blood and great ones and ignored its implications.
The narrator frames every Bloodborne boss as a human story expressing suffering caused by systemic institutional failures rather than simple monster encounters.
